responseText:
Action items (extracted & suggested owners, priorities, and rough deadlines)

1) Investigate recurring Friday-afternoon deploy failures
- Tasks: collect deploy logs/CI output for recent failures, reproduce in staging, identify root cause, implement fix and a rollback plan, add monitoring/alerts for the deploy window.
- Owner: DevOps/Platform team (or a named SRE/DevOps lead)
- Priority: High
- Deadline: RCA within 5 business days; fix/mitigation within 10 business days.

2) Clarify staging DB ownership and runbook
- Tasks: assign a single owner or rotating on-call for the staging DB, create/update a runbook covering access, backups, restore steps, maintenance windows, and escalation contacts.
- Owner: Engineering manager (with the owner designated from platform/backend team)
- Priority: High
- Deadline: Owner assigned and runbook drafted within 3 business days; runbook finalized within 7 days.

3) Create and enforce a pre-merge checklist (QA request)
- Tasks: draft checklist (tests to run, required approvals, environment verification, data migrations, rollback steps), add checklist to PR template, require checklist items in CI or code-review gate where possible.
- Owner: QA lead + Engineering leads
- Priority: High
- Deadline: Draft within 3 business days; integrate into PR workflow within 7–10 days.

4) Improve deploy/process ownership and scheduling
- Tasks: define who is responsible for production/staging deploys (including Friday sign-off), consider avoiding risky deploys on Friday afternoons or require additional approvals, document deploy schedule/guardrails.
- Owner: Release manager / Engineering leadership
- Priority: Medium–High
- Deadline: Policy documented within 7 days.

5) Address standup attendance & communication gaps
- Tasks: confirm expectations for standups (attendance, remote sign-in, async updates), capture recurring absences, propose fallback coverage, consider recording or a short async status channel for those who must miss.
- Owner: Scrum master / Team lead
- Priority: Medium
- Deadline: Clarify policy and communicate to team within 3 business days.

6) Follow up on Marcus’s recent absences/early leaves
- Tasks: manager to have a private, supportive check-in with Marcus to understand circumstances (and offer accommodations or referrals as needed); log occurrences and agreed next steps; arrange temporary coverage if his absences impact deliverables.
- Owner: Marcus’s manager / people manager
- Priority: High (because of repeated pattern)
- Deadline: Manager reaches out within 1 business day.

What I can (and cannot) say about Marcus
- I cannot determine from these notes whether Marcus is dealing with a personal/home issue or a health problem. Inferring health or personal circumstances from attendance notes would be speculation and could be sensitive.
- Recommended next step: have a private, respectful conversation to ask if he’s okay and whether he needs support or accommodations. If you want, involve HR or Employee Assistance Program (EAP) resources depending on company policy.

Suggested short message template manager can use
- "Hey Marcus — I noticed you missed a couple of standups and left early the past few days. Are you doing okay? If there's anything you need (flex time, workload help, or support), I'm here to help — we can chat privately whenever you're available."

If you want, I can:
- Draft the pre-merge checklist template or PR checklist text.
- Draft a private manager message tailored to your tone.
- Propose a deploy-runbook checklist for Friday-safe deployment practices. Which would you like next?
